newsitem.title: USA: Thorn Apple Valley cites savings, margins.
newsitem.headline: Thorn Apple Valley cites savings, margins.

text.p: Thorn Apple Valley said Thursday that facility improvements and sales of higher-margin products helped it to report a second quarter profit of $2 million, or $0.33 a share.
But Thorn Apple Valley President Joel Dorfman said achieving improvment in the company's fresh pork division is a "longer term prospect" because of an inadequate hog supply.
"Based on the most recent pig crop report, there is little reason to expect improved profitability in this segment during the remainder of the fiscal year," Dorfman said.
Thorn Apple Valley's current fiscal year ends in June.

For the second quarter ended December 13, the company said its sales volume of fresh pork, in pounds, was down about five percent from the year-ago period because of the shortage of market hogs. Raw material prices have outpaced increases in selling prices for the division.
"We are hopeful, however, that the recent high level of hog producer profitability will encourage expanded hog production," Dorfman said.
He added that Thorn Apple is continues to improve efficiencies at its fresh pork plant.

The company's overall $2 million profit for the second fiscal quarter, due largely to improvements in its processed meats division, compared with a year-earlier loss of about $1.8 million, or $0.30 a share.
Thorn Apple said its processed meat results improved because of cost reductions made possible by its strategic acquisition, consolidation, construction and renovation of certain facilities.
Productivity at the Forrest City, Ark., hot dog plant improved by 40 percent this year, Thorn Apple said.

"Increased consumer demand during the holiday season for our spiral sliced and boneless hams also contributed to improved performance," Dorfman said. "We were particularly pleased with the strong demand for our recently acquired Corn King and Wilson Certified brands."
